appraisal_events.evidence: cette maladie qu'était l'amour de Swann avait tellement multiplié... qu'on n'aurait pas pu l'arracher de lui sans le détruire lui-même à peu près tout entier: comme on dit en chirurgie, son amour n'était plus opérable.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator frames Swann's love for Odette as an incurable, all-consuming illness fused inseparably with his whole being, so that he can no longer resist its pull or separate himself from it; this is a sustained, narrator-endorsed diminishment of his self-possession and autonomy.

status_effects.explanation: Swann is shown helplessly oscillating between resolutions to separate from Odette and irresistible relapses into needing to see her, with the narrator stressing that he has lost the will and capacity to resist.

The extended clinical comparison to a morphine addict or consumptive patient misunderstood by his doctor casts Swann in a pathological, diminished light, no longer master of his own judgment or reactions.
